Meteorological forecasting system 
*341. SHRI R. P. GO ENKA: Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have analysed the shortcomings in the present 
meteorological forecasting system; 

RAJYA SABHA [19 August, 2004] 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is a fact that a proposal has been formulated to procure some hi-tech 
world class equipment worth Rs. 500 crores to secure bettei overall meteorological 
forecasting and even for district-wise predictions; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and its present status? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table 
of the House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Monsoon rainfall over the Indian peninsula is a result of several 
natural phenomena occurring across the globe. With the present day observational 
infrastructure and technology the world over, it is not possible to make predictions on 
spatial and temporal variations of the monsoon activity. However, on the basis of 
observations, patterns of rainfall across the country can be identified for making useful 
forecasts. The Indian Meteorological Department has been monitoring rainfall across 
the country since a long time and has already evolved models for forecasting the total 
seasonal rainfall as well as making short range forecast for meteorological sub-divisions. 
These forecasts have given important guidance to our operations, in particular, the 
agriculture operations. For improving forecasts, new models are always being 
introduced and used. 
(c) and (d) The process of upgradation of the observational systems is continuous. 
Better observations will help in improving the modeling for better forecasts. But as this 
process is evolutionary in nature, no time frame can be fixed for the same. Indian 
Meteorological Department (IMD) has come out with a proposal for investing Rs. 500 
Crores in some important areas for improving observations and the forecast system. The 
proposal is being submitted for consideration of the Government. As already stated 
complexities of weather patterns over the Indian sub continent make it extremely 
difficult to make forecasts about small geographical regions like Districts.

SHRI AMAR SINGH:

Statement 
(a) It is estimated that about 5000 Indians are presently in Iraq. At least 13

(b) and (c) Government have decided to provide all possible help to Indians in Iraq 
who want to return to India. In this connection, the Government have taken the* 
following concrete steps and steps:— 
(i) Government has instructed the Indian Missions in Iraq and its 
neighbouring countries to extend all possible assistance to the Indian 
nationals in Iraq who want to return to India. 
(ii) Government has requested the Governments of Jordan and Kuwait to issue 
transit visas for Indians returning to India from Iraq. 
(iii) Indian Mission in Baghdad has contacted the employers of Indians who 
wish to return to India to facilitate their travel out of Iraq and settlement of 
their dues by their employers. 
(iv) The Indian Embassy in Baghdad has sent its officials to some of the places in 
Iraq where the Indians are located to enquire their well-being and to 
provide assistance and guidance in case they have decided to leave 
Iraq. 
(d) and (e) On the night of 21stJuly, 2004, it was learnt from a news agency report 
that three Indian nationals identified as Antaryami Bains, Tilak Raj and Sukhdev Singh 
were among the seven persons taken hostage by an Iraqi group identified as 'The Holders of 
the Black Banners". The hostages included in addition three Kenyans and one Egyptian. They 
were all employed as heavy vechicle drivers by the Kuwait based company, Kuwait and Gulf 
Link Transport Co. (KGLTC). The kidnappers in a statement reported by the media 
demanded withdrawal of all citizens 
8

belonging to the countries of the hostages from Iraq including troops and an end 
to the activities of the transport company in Iraq. The Group threatened to 
behead a hostage every 72 hours unless these demands are met. 
Immediately after the hostage taking was reported, the Government 
initiated action forthwith to secure their release. Senior officials of the 
Ministry of External Affairs contacted Indian Missions in Baghdad and 
Kuwait to explore all possiblities to ensure safety of the hostages and their 
early release. Minister of State (MoS) for External Affairs, Shri E. Ahammed 
spoke to the Charged Affaires in Embassy of India, Baghdad and the Indian 
Ambassador in Kuwait. A Crisis Management Group was constituted under the 
Chairmanship of Shri Ahammed and a Control Room was made operative in 
Ministry of External Affairs. Minister of External Affairs, Shri K. Natwar 
Singh issued an appeal to the kidnappers through the Arab TV Network for 
release of the hostages who are innocent civilians and not combatants. The 
Government also contacted the Governments of Egypt and Kenya whose 
nationals are among the hostages for inputs to work for the release of the 
hostages. Our Mission in Kuwait has been in touch with the transport company 
KGL from the very beginning of the abduction and received and assured the 
company that it will take all possible steps to secure release and safe return of 
the kidnapped drivers. 
The situation is constantly being monitored by the Crisis Management 
Group which meets several times a day to review strategies to secure safe and 
early release of hostages. Shri E. Ah ammed, MOS has issued two appeals to 
the kidnappers through Arabic TV network highlighting historical relations 
between India and Iraq and India's well-known and principled position and 
concern for the welfare and well being of Iraqi people and their country and 
requesting for immediate release of the hostages. He also made an appeal to the 
captors in Arabic language for release of the hostages on humanitarian grounds. 
Religious leaders in Iraq and other Gulf countries were contacted to intercede 
for the release of the hostages. Ambassador of India in Muscat, Shri Talmiz 
Ahmad alongwith an Arabic interpreter has been deputed to Iraq to monitor and 
report on the development and to assist in the work of the Indian mission for 
early and safe release of the hostages. Cabinet Secretary chaired several 
meetings to review the situation and the ongoing efforts to secure the release of 
the hostages. Prime Minister held a meeting to

Engineering, Electrical Engineering and Mechanical Engineering as optional 
Subjects. Computer Science is, however, not included in the list of optional

THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI DAYANIDHI MARAN): (a) The 
Telecommunications Tariff Order (TTO), 1999 provides flexibility to all 
cellular operators including BSNL & MTNL to fix tariffs. Thus, the operators are 
at liberty to offer alternate tariff packages to subscriber depending upon their 
usage pattern. There are a large number of tariff plans offered by MTNL, BSNL 
and other cellular operators. Since there are too many combinations of rentals 
and airtime charges in various alternative packages, the tariff levels of MTNL 
and BSNL vis-a-vis other private cellular operators, do not provide 
comparable data for any meaningful conclusion. A broad comparison of one 
of the tariffs plan for general public of BSNL, MTNL and sample private 
operator has been made. It is observed that BSNL plan charges Rs. 225.00 as 
monthly rental, local call charge of Rs. 2.20 & STD call charge of Rs. 2.40 to 
3.60 per minute depending upon distance but with a pulse rate of 15 seconds and 
national SMS charge of Rs. 0.40 per message. The MTNL has a plan with Rs. 
100.00 as monthly rental, local call charge of Rs. 1.90 per minute & STD call 
charge of Rs. 1.90 to 3.90 per minute depending upon distance & type of 
terminating network with 60 seconds pul se and national SMS charge of Rs. 
1.50 per message. The private operator has a plan of

per message. A sample tariff plan each of MTNL and BSNL are given in the

1628. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be

4,000 crores of foreign direct investment in mining sector;

MINES (DR. DASARI NARAYAN RAO): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB), in consultation with 
the Department of Mines, has so far approved 73 proposals of Foreign Direct 
Investment (FDI) in the mining sector. The likely investment in these cases 
will be about Rs.4,044 crores. The approval granted by FIPB is only for foreign 
equity participation in a company incorporated in India. After obtaining FIPB 
approval these companies are required to apply to the concerned State 
Governments, which are the owners of minerals in their respective territorial 
jurisdictions for mineral concessions. 
(c) Yes, Sir. The geological setting and metallogenitic history of India is 
similar to mineral rich Australia, South Africa and Antarctica. However, due to 
low investment and lack of advanced state-of-the-art technology for detailed 
exploration, deep-seated high value minerals like gold, diamond, base metals, 
etc. have not yet been fully discovered. 
(d) and (e) The Government already offers a wide range of incentives to 
investors in India, engaged in mining activities. The entire non-atomic and non-
fuel mining sector is now open for private investment including Foreign Direct 
Investment (FDI). A hundred per cent FDI is permitted for mineral exploration 
through the automatic route except diamonds and precious stones where 
100% is permitted through Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB). The 
other incentives inter alia include (a) availability of tax holiday; (b) 
depreciation allowances on mining and quarrying equipments, environment 
protection equipment, pollution control equipment, energy saving equipment, 
etc.; (c) deduction in respect of export turnover; and (d) limited deduction of 
expenditure on prospecting, extraction and production of minerals from the 
total income.

Seeping of sea water in Neyveli 
1633. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that there is a fear of seeping in sea 
water in Neyveli region of Tamil Nadu due to pumping out of huge quantity of 
water from the Neyveli Lignite Corporation's mines; 
(b) whether Government have conducted any survey to investigate the 
matter; and 
(c) whether there are any norms with regard to the pumping of water from 
deep mines? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL AND 
MINES (DR. DASARI NARAYAN RAO): (a) Yes, Sir. The Government is 
aware of the possibility of seeping in of sea water due to pumping out of water 
from mines. 
(b) The Central Ground Water Board, at the request of Neyveli Lignite 
Corporation Ltd. (NLC), has put up observation wells along the coast to 
continuously monitor any salt water intrusion from sea to inland and the studies 
made so far indicate that there is no such occurrence. NLC has also requested 
Geological Survey of India to undertake scientific studies in Neyveli region so as 
to understand seeping of sea water, if any, due to pumping by NLC for mining 
operations, agriculturists and other industries operating in the region. 
(c) Yes, Sir. Ministry of Environment and Forests and the Central 
Ground Water Board have prescribed the limits restricting ground water 
pumping from NLC's mines. NLC is pumping ground water to the extent it has 
been permitted by the above agencies.

issues of mutual concern and interest, including strategic issues, defence,

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI E. AHAMMED): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) On the night of 21st July, 2004, it was learnt from a news agency report 
that three Indian nationals identified as Antaryami Bains, Tilak Raj and Sukhdev 
Singh were among the seven persons taken hostages by an Iraqi group 
identified as "The Holders of the Black  Banners".The hostages included in 
addition three Kenyans and one Egyptian. They were all employed as heavy 
vehicle drivers by the Kuwait based company, Kuwait and Gulf Link Transport Co. 
(KGL). The kidnappers in a  statement reported by the media demanded 
withdrawal of all citizens belonging to the countries of the hostages from Iraq 
including troops and an end to the activities of the transport company in Iraq. 
The group threatened to behead a hostage every 72 hours unless these 
demands are met. 
(c) No, Sir. 
(d) Immediately after the hostage taking was reported, the 
Government initiated action forthwith to secure their release. Senior 
officials of the Ministry of External  Affairs contacted Indian Missions in 
Baghdad and Kuwait to explore all possibilities to ensure safety of the 
hostages and their early release. Mini ster of State (MoS) for External 
Affairs, Shri E. Ahammed spoke to the Charge d" Affairs in Embassy of 
India, Baghdad and the Indian Ambassador in Kuwait. A Crisis 
Management Group was constituted under the Chairmanship of Shri E. 
Ahammed, MoS and a Control Room was made operative in Ministry of 
External Affairs. Minister of External Affairs, Shri K. Natwar Singh, issued 
112 

[19 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
an appeal to the kidnappers through Arab TV channel for release of the hostages 
who are innocent civilians and not combatants. The Government also contacted 
the Governments of Egypt and Kenya whose nationals are among the hostages 
for inputs to work for" the release of the hostages. Our Mission in Kuwait has 
been in touch with the transport company KGL from the very beginning of the 
abduction and received an assurance from the company to take all possible steps 
to ensure release and safe return of the kidnapped drivers. The situation is 
constantly being monitored by the Crisis Management Group which meets 
regularly and frequently to review strategies to secure safe and early release of 
hostages. Shri E. Ahammed, MoS has issued appeals to the kidnappers 
through Arabic TV network highlighting historical relations between India and 
Iraq and India's well-known and princi pled position and concern for the 
welfare and well-being of Iraqi people  and their country and requesting for 
immediate release of the hostages. He also made an appeal to the captors in Arabic 
language for release of the hostages on humanitarian grounds. Religious leaders 
in Iraq and other Gulf countries were contacted to intercede for the release of 
the hostages. Ambassador of India in Muscat, Shri Talmiz Ahmad alongwith an 
Arabic interpreter has been deputed to Iraq to monitor and report on the 
developments and to assist in the work of the Indian Mission for early and 
safe release of the hostages. Cabinet Secretary has been regularly holding 
inter-Ministerial/ Departmental meetings to review the situation and the 
ongoing efforts to secure the releas e of the hostages. External Affairs 
Minister has been following developments closely and giving directions 
whenever necessary. The Prime Minister and the CCPA have also held 
meetings to review developments. Effort s are continuing to get their release. 
The deadline set by the kidnappers has been extended several times and the 
talks between the transport compan y KGL and the kidnappers through 
mediators are continuing.

Banners". The hostages included in addition three Kenyans and one Egyptian.

RAJYA SABHA [19 August, 2004] 
(c) Immediately after the hostage taking was reported, the Government 
initiated action forthwith to secure their release. Senior officials of the Ministry of 
External Affairs contacted Indian Missions in Baghdad and Kuwait to explore all 
possibilities to ensure safety of the hostages and their early release. Minister of State 
(MoS) for External Affairs, Shri E. Ahammed spoke to the Charge d'Affairs in 
Embassy of India, Baghdad and the Indian Ambassador in Kuwait. A Crisis 
Management Group was constituted under the Chairmanship of Shri Ahammed (MoS) 
and a Control Room was made operative in Ministry of External Affairs. Minister of 
External Affairs, Shri K. Natwar Singh appealed to the kidnappers through Arab TV

Government also contacted the Governments of Egypt and Kenya whose nationals are 
among the hostages for inputs to work for the release of the hostages. Our Mission in 
Kuwait has been in touch with the transport company KGL from the very begining of 
the abduction and received assurance from the company that it will take all possible 
steps to ensure release and safe return of the kidnapped drivers. 
The situation is constantly being monitored by the Crisis Management 
Group which meets regularly and frequently 4o review strategies to secure safe and early 
release of hostages. Shri E. Ahammed, MoS has issued two appeals to the kidnappers through 
Arabic TV network highlighting historical relations between India and Iraq and India's 
well-known and principled position and concern for the welfare and well-being of Iraqi 
people and their country and requesting for immediate release of the hostages. He also 
made an appeal to the captors in Arabic language for release of the hostages on 
humanitarian grounds. Religious leaders in Iraq and other Gulf countries were contacted to 
intercede for the release of the hostages. Ambassador of India in Muscat, Shri Talmiz Ahmad 
along with an Arabic interpreter has been deputed to Iraq to monitor and report on the 
developments and to assist in the work of the Indian mission for early and safe release of 
the hostages. Cabinet Secretary has been regularly holding inter-
Ministerial/Departmental meetings to review the situation and the ongoing efforts to 
secure the release of the hostages. External Affairs Minister has been following 
developments closely and giving directions whenever necessary. The Prime Minister and 
the CCPA have also held meeting to review developments.

of the employment/plight of the child labour. They have not found child 
labour under fourteen years of age working in the mines of Rajasthan during 
their inspections.

implementing the scheme of National Child Labour Project (NCLP) in 
various child labour endemic districts in State of Rajasthan for children

1772. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Meteorological Department has badly failed 
in forecasting weather and its estimates have always been proving wrong; 
184 

[19 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor, 
(c) whether any measures have been ta ken to ensure correct forecasts 
by the Meteorological Department; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) No, Sir. IMD has been 
using 16-parameter Power Regression Model for issuing Long Range 
Forecast of total quantum of rainfall likely during the season as a whole since 
1988. Its performance was seen to be satisfactory and was appreciated until 
2002 when the model could not capture the large deficiency of rainfall. 
(b) Monsoon is a complex phenomenon involving land, ocean and 
atmosphere. It originates as a result of  series of energy exchanges occurring 
in the earth atmosphere system. Though  attempts have been made over the 
year to unravel the mysteries of development and strengthening of monsoon, 
the complex interactions leading to energy exchange are not well understood. 
There is no technology anywhere in the world to give exact forecast of 
monsoon like systems. 
(c) and (d) Attempts were made to refine and introduce a number of 
new models before commencement of 2003 monsoon. These models gave 
fairly accurate forecasts for the seas on and also for the month of July 2003. 
However, based on the same models, the forecasts for rainfall in July 2004 has 
not Materialized as the realised rainfall was 81% compared to 98+9% 
forecasted rainfall. Seasonal rainfall forecast is 100+4%. The performance for 
the season will be assessed after the season is over. IMD in collaboration with 
Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore has implemented a Numerical Weather 
Prediction (NWP) system for the seasonal prediction of monsoon rainfall. 
Currently the NWP system is in the experimental mode and some
